angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 532,211 km at 169.07 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.9147 +/- 0.0191 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10): 169.07 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.765 +/- 0.024 solar radii from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-203 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract): 532,211 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.793 +/- 0.033 solar masses from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-203 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5026 +/- 82 K from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-203 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-203 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-203.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.570, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
